claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNiTi elemental powder mixture has high surface area and potential surface oxides.
CoCrFeNiTi tends to form HCP phases during slow cooling or conventional sintering because of Ti segregation.
High-energy mechanical alloying induces severe plastic deformation and promotes solid-solution formation.
Milling under argon limits oxygen and carbon contamination.

SPS at 900–1000 °C, a heating rate above 100 °C/min, and a dwell below 10 minutes kinetically traps a dominant FCC solid solution with minor BCC precipitates while preventing HCP and intermetallic formation.
High-energy milling followed by rapid SPS suppresses porosity in CoCrFeNiTi.
Controlling the SPS displacement rate prevents cracking caused by thermal-expansion mismatch.
Milling creates severe lattice distortion and a high dislocation density.
Suppressed diffusion during rapid sintering hinders HCP nucleation and promotes retention of metastable FCC.
Limiting thermal exposure prevents Ti segregation in CoCrFeNiTi.
High applied pressure and rapid SPS densification eliminate porosity.
Minor BCC precipitates arise from kinetically trapped local compositional fluctuations or solute clustering before brittle intermetallics can coarsen.
The proposed process produces more than 98% theoretical density.
The processed alloy has significantly greater hardness than its cast counterpart because of grain refinement and solid-solution strengthening.
Avoiding HCP and Laves phases avoids their associated brittleness.
Conventional casting of CoCrFeNiTi gives a porous, soft, single-phase FCC baseline.
Conventional sintering is associated with porosity and embrittlement.
Above approximately 1100 °C, thermodynamic HCP stability overtakes the kinetic barrier in Ti-rich systems.
Keeping oxygen below approximately 0.5–1.0 wt% avoids stabilization of the alpha-HCP phase.
Oxide or carbide contamination introduced during milling can strengthen the alloy while reducing ductility.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says that short thermal exposure suppresses HCP nucleation, so a greater HCP fraction after extending the dwell to 60 minutes would support the proposed kinetic mechanism. The falsification rule instead declares an HCP increase above 20% under the extended dwell to be falsifying.

The predicted outcome attributes hardness jointly to grain refinement and solid-solution strengthening, while the requested attribution test is framed as grain refinement rather than solute strengthening. The experiment has no composition-matched or grain-size-matched control capable of separating these contributions.
